extracted.intended_audience: NSW HSC English markers, teachers and senior English students
extracted.subtask_description: Marking guidelines for the 2011 NSW Higher School Certificate English (Standard and Advanced) Paper 1 Area of Study, specifying criteria and banded descriptors for short-answer, creative writing and extended-response questions on belonging and places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1(a) — explain how a visual text offers a perspective on belonging
rubrics_metrics.description: Selects one aspect of the visual text and explains how it offers a perspective on belonging; Attempts to explain how the visual text offers a perspective on belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks: 2 = Selects one aspect of the visual text and explains how it offers a perspective on belonging (clear, focused explanation). 1 = Attempts to explain how the visual text offers a perspective on belonging (limited or partial explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1(b) — explain how personal insights into belonging are conveyed
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains how personal insights into belonging to places are conveyed in the transcript; Attempts to explain or explains in a limited way how personal insights into belonging to places are conveyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks: 2 = Explanation of how personal insights into belonging to places are conveyed (clear and relevant). 1 = Attempt or limited explanation (vague or underdeveloped).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1(c) — what a character comes to understand about belonging (textual references required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates, with aptly chosen textual references, what Jack comes to understand about belonging; Demonstrates, with some textual references, what Jack comes to understand about belonging; Describes aspects of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks: 3 = Demonstrates with aptly chosen textual references (detailed, well-supported explanation of Jack's understanding). 2 = Demonstrates with some textual references (adequate support). 1 = Describes aspects of the text (limited or descriptive only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1(d) — importance of memories to a character's sense of belonging (textual references required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discusses effectively, with aptly chosen textual references, the importance of memories to Eilis’s sense of belonging; Discusses, with some textual references, the importance of memories to Eilis’s sense of belonging; Describes aspects of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks: 3 = Effective discussion with aptly chosen textual references (insightful and well-supported). 2 = Discussion with some textual references (adequate). 1 = Description of aspects of the text (limited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1(e) — analyse relationship between places and identity in two texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses effectively the relationship between places and identity in TWO of the texts; Analyses adequately the relationship between places and identity in TWO of the texts; Demonstrates limited/some understanding of the relationship between places and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks: 5 = Effective analysis of the relationship between places and identity in two texts (insightful, well-structured, well-supported). Marks 3–4 = Adequate analysis in two texts (clear but less developed). Marks 1–2 = Limited or partial understanding of the relationship (underdeveloped, descriptive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2 (Section II) — creative writing: remembered places and belonging
rubrics_metrics.description: Composes skilfully/an engaging piece of creative writing that captures the significance of remembered places to the experience of belonging; Skilfully/Effectively/ Adequately explores the experience of belonging; Demonstrates skilful/effective/adequate/limited/elementary control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and selected form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks bands: 13–15 = Composes skilfully an engaging piece that captures significance of remembered places; skilfully explores belonging; demonstrates skilful control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and selected form. 10–12 = Composes effectively an engaging piece; effectively explores belonging; demonstrates effective control of language and structure. 7–9 = Composes a piece focusing on remembered places and belonging; explores aspects of belonging; demonstrates adequate control of language and structure. 4–6 = Attempts to compose; attempts to explore belonging; demonstrates limited control and limited appropriateness. 1–3 = Attempts to compose a response; demonstrates elementary control of language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3 (Section III) — extended response: perceptions of belonging influenced by connections to places
rubrics_metrics.description: Explores skilfully/effectively/how perceptions of belonging and not belonging can be influenced by connections to places; Presents a skilful/effective/adequate response with well-chosen/ap­tly chosen/appropriate textual references from the prescribed text and at least one other related text; Composes a well-integrated/effective/adequate response using language appropriate to audience, purpose and context; Demonstrates limited understanding or elementary reference at lower bands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks bands: 13–15 = Explores skilfully how perceptions of belonging and not belonging are influenced by connections to places; presents a skilful response with well-chosen detailed textual references from the prescribed text and at least one other related text; composes a well-integrated response using appropriate language. 10–12 = Explores effectively; presents an effective response with aptly chosen textual references from prescribed and at least one related text; composes an effective response using appropriate language. 7–9 = Explores how perceptions can be influenced; presents a response using appropriate textual references from prescribed and at least one other related text; composes an adequate response using appropriate language. 4–6 = Demonstrates limited understanding of perceptions of belonging; describes aspects of the texts; attempts a response with limited appropriateness and elementary referencing. 1–3 = Attempts to compose a response (minimal development).
